title: Former Intel packaging chief Navid Shahriari joins MediaTek as senior vice president
content: MediaTek announced that Navid Shahriari will join the company on November 9 as Senior Vice President, reporting to the General Manager and Chief Operating Officer.

title: Waymo fleet crowds San Diego chargers, straining EV access
content: Alphabet's autonomous taxi service Waymo began operations in San Diego, California, in September 2026 and expanded its coverage on October 27. However, EV owners have reported that large numbers of robotaxis are using public fast-charging stations, forcing other drivers to queue and prompting local politicians to call for tighter oversight of autonomous vehicles.

title: Amazon's US$2 billion Ohio data center plan faces new hurdle as voters approve ban
content: Voters in Sunbury, Ohio, approved a ban on large data centers in the November 3 election, raising a new obstacle to Amazon's proposed US$2 billion project as communities across the US move to restrict AI infrastructure development.

title: US election previews shift toward AI oversight and data center regulation
content: Asian stocks wavered on November 4 in response to the US midterm election results. While the final votes are still being counted, current results show the Democratic Party winning majorities in both the House of Representatives and Senate, a clear indication of voters' discontent about data center development in their localities, which could usher in more regulation of the AI industry.

title: Innodisk advances AI data center push with eSSD, DDR5 products
content: Industrial memory module maker Innodisk is deepening its AI data center strategy by supplying critical components for AI infrastructure, including enterprise solid-state drives (eSSDs) and AI server memory modules. title: Raydium faces 4Q26 slowdown after AI capacity fears fuel customer stockpiling
content: Display driver IC designer Raydium Semiconductor reported consolidated revenue of NT$6.57 billion (≈ US$200 million) for the third quarter of 2026, down 3.8% sequentially but up 21.0% year on year. Gross margin reached 26.4%, rising 0.7pp from the previous quarter but falling 2.2pp from a year earlier. Operating profit declined 13.1% sequentially and 11.7% year on year to NT$310 million.

title: Broadcom loses final appeal over Samsung chip supply deal
content: South Korea's Supreme Court has upheld a KRW18.664 billion (approx. US$13.9 million) fine against Broadcom for pressuring Samsung Electronics into a long-term smartphone component purchasing agreement by disrupting supplies, bringing the US chipmaker's legal challenge to an end.

title: Onsemi to buy Ferric for US$600M to strengthen AI processor power delivery
content: Onsemi has agreed to acquire Ferric, Inc., a developer of integrated voltage regulator (IVR) technology, for US$600 million in cash plus up to US$175 million in contingent consideration tied to revenue milestones, the company announced on November 2, 2026. Alongside the deal, Onsemi raised its 2030 AI data center revenue target by US$500 million to more than US$3 billion.

title: Weblink International posts record 3Q26 profit on AI demand
content: Weblink International Inc. reported record profit for both the third quarter of 2026 and the first three quarters, driven by growing enterprise AI adoption and sales of new products. The company's board approved its third-quarter 2026 financial report on November 3.

title: Global chip sales top US$500 billion in a single quarter for first time
content: Worldwide semiconductor revenue reached US$517.7 billion in the third quarter of 2026, a 24.1% increase from the prior quarter, according to data released by the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) on Tuesday.

title: Marvell's Lumentum deal gives optical DSP rivals until 2028 to court its customers
content: Marvell's proposed all-stock acquisition of Lumentum faces a challenge beyond a shrinking takeover premium: whether optical module makers will shift orders away from its dominant optical digital signal processor (DSP) business.

title: CHT expands Google partnership with AI services
content: Chunghwa Telecom (CHT) is expanding its partnership with Google beyond Google One, YouTube Premium and Pixel smartphone sales to include GenAI services. On November 4, CHT announced plans to introduce Google's latest AI offerings through its channels, while Google Taiwan said the partners will launch more initiatives in 2027 to promote AI-enabled living.

title: Intel reportedly targets DDR4 upgrades with Raptor Lake Next
content: DDR4 memory, once gradually fading from the market, is regaining popularity as tight DRAM supply drives DDR5 prices higher. Following AMD's revival of processors supporting the AM4 platform, Intel is reportedly preparing to extend its Raptor Lake architecture to target the DDR4 PC upgrade market.

title: GCS Holdings welcomes Marvell's Lumentum deal, locks in 2027 InP supply
content: Marvell Technology and optical communications laser maker Lumentum announced on November 2 that they had signed a definitive agreement for Marvell to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction. Compound semiconductor maker GCS welcomed the deal, saying it will give Marvell's optoelectronics business a more complete product portfolio.

title: Samsung to reportedly make AMD, Nvidia HBM base dies at second Texas fab
content: Samsung Electronics plans to produce high-bandwidth memory (HBM) base dies for AMD at its second foundry plant in Taylor, Texas, with the US chipmaker accounting for most of the facility's planned output, South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper reported on November 3, citing industry sources. The report said the plant would also supply Nvidia, although Samsung has not confirmed either customer's orders.

title: PC slump hits Darfon, but MLCCs, green energy keep 2026 growth on track
content: Affected by weak notebook and PC demand, Darfon Electronics reported third-quarter 2026 consolidated revenue of NT$7.011 billion (US$214 million), up 7.8% year-over-year but down about 6.7% quarter-over-quarter. The company said notebook and PC demand weakened after higher raw material and component costs pushed up end-product prices, dragging down its IT peripherals business, which accounts for about 40% of revenue.
